values: A stakeholder decision workbook for the proposed Java / Spring Boot custom-agent platform

Working agreement: resolve all blocking questions, record one accountable owner, and mark a row Decided only after stakeholder approval. Recommended defaults are implementation assumptions—not silent decisions.

1. Filter the Questions tab by Primary stakeholder and Blocking?.  2. Enter a concrete response, decision owner, and due date.  3. Use In Review while validating and Blocked only when a named dependency exists.  4. Change Status to Decided after approval.  5. Review this Overview tab until all Blocking decisions are resolved.
WebEngage Custom Agents — Stakeholder Clarification Tracker
Complete all Critical / Blocking questions before implementation. Yellow columns are stakeholder-owned inputs.
Generated 31 Jul 2026  •  72 questions  •  Update one accountable decision owner per row
When users ‘write their own agents,’ what artifact will they provide?
Choose one: declarative definition; Java source upload; compiled JAR/plugin; or Java classes deployed with this service. Recommended: declarative definitions with trusted Java tool components.
Platform Architecture; Security / IAM; Backend Engineering
The choice determines deployment, isolation, security, and lifecycle architecture.
Must new or updated agents become available without rebuilding or restarting the service?
Recommended: yes for declarative definitions; controlled deployment for trusted Java extensions.
Clarifies whether runtime registration and hot reload are required.
Do agents require draft, published, and versioned states, or should every update become active immediately?
Recommended: Draft → Published → Retired with immutable published versions.
Defines safe authoring, rollback, and audit behavior.
Can an agent invoke any registered tool, or only an explicit per-agent allowlist?
Recommended: explicit allowlist, validated at publish and run time.
Controls privilege boundaries and limits unintended actions.
Should each agent define an input and output JSON Schema?
Recommended: yes; require input schema and allow optional output schema.
Enables validation, discoverability, and stable API contracts.
Can agents store configuration or secrets, and how should secrets be represented?
Recommended: store non-secret configuration; reference secrets by vault identifier only.
Prevents credentials from leaking into definitions and transcripts.
What is the Core Agentic Layer endpoint, HTTP method, and request/response contract?
Provide OpenAPI or representative request/response examples, including errors.
The orchestration client cannot be implemented without a stable contract.
Is the tool-calling protocol OpenAI-compatible or WebEngage-specific?
Recommended: document a versioned internal contract even if it mirrors OpenAI tool calling.
Determines message types, tool-call parsing, and compatibility strategy.
Should this service perform the full agent loop: send context, receive tool calls, execute tools, return results, and repeat until a final answer?
Recommended: yes; the custom-agent service owns tool execution and the Core Agentic Layer owns model generation.
Core Agentic Layer; Core Platform / Tool Owners
Establishes the service boundary and orchestration responsibility.
What maximum iterations, wall-clock timeout, token limit, and cost limit should apply per execution?
Recommended starting point: 10 iterations, 5-minute timeout, configurable token/cost ceilings.
Prevents runaway loops and unbounded latency or spend.
Should multiple tool calls returned in one model response execute in parallel?
Recommended: parallel only for tools declared read-only and concurrency-safe.
Core Platform / Tool Owners; Backend Engineering
Affects performance, ordering, and side-effect safety.
Should conversation context persist across separate executions or only within one run?
Recommended: isolate by run initially; add explicit conversation/session IDs if cross-run continuity is needed.
Determines storage model, privacy scope, and context assembly.
Is a mock Core Agentic Layer acceptable for local development and automated tests?
Recommended: yes, with deterministic scripted tool-call scenarios.
Enables reliable development and integration testing without model dependency.
What are the initial tools and their request/response contracts?
Provide tool names, descriptions, JSON schemas, owners, side-effect classification, and examples.
Tool definitions are foundational inputs to agent configuration and execution.
How are core-platform tools exposed: HTTP, gRPC, Kafka, Java SDKs, or a combination?
Document the protocol and service endpoint for each initial tool.
Drives connector abstractions, error handling, and deployment dependencies.
How should this service authenticate to core platforms: service credentials, delegated user identity, or both?
Recommended: service identity plus delegated user/account context where authorization requires it.
Core Platform / Tool Owners; Platform Architecture
Defines downstream trust and least-privilege enforcement.
Are tools synchronous, asynchronous, or mixed?
Classify every initial tool and define polling or callback behavior for asynchronous tools.
Determines orchestration state transitions and execution persistence.
Should failed tool calls be retried, and which operations are safe to retry?
Recommended: retry only idempotent operations; require idempotency keys for retryable writes.
Avoids duplicate side effects while improving resilience.
Do sensitive or high-impact tools require human confirmation or approval before execution?
Recommended: risk-tier tools and require approval for destructive, external, or high-volume actions.
Product; Core Platform / Tool Owners; Data Privacy / Compliance
Should the framework expose a standard Java tool interface and registry for tools implemented as Spring beans?
Recommended: yes, with metadata, input schema, authorization hook, execution method, and result schema.
Backend Engineering; Core Platform / Tool Owners
Creates a consistent extension model and test surface.
Which API capabilities are required in the first release?
Confirm: agent CRUD/list; publish/version; run; status/result; cancel; run/transcript history; schedule CRUD and enable/disable.
Fixes the external API scope and delivery boundary.
Should execution be synchronous, asynchronous, or both?
Recommended: both; asynchronous by default and synchronous with a strict timeout.
Determines response semantics, persistence, and worker design.
What should an execution trigger contain besides agent ID?
Confirm arbitrary JSON input, user context, account/license identifier, correlation ID, and idempotency key.
Defines validation, tenancy, tracing, and replay protection.
Should deleted agents be soft-deleted for auditability?
Recommended: soft delete, with admin-only purge subject to retention policy.
Balances audit requirements with eventual data deletion.
What pagination, sorting, and filtering conventions should the REST APIs follow?
Provide WebEngage standards; otherwise use cursor pagination for runs and page/size for agent administration.
Is REST with OpenAPI/Swagger sufficient, or is another API style required?
Recommended: versioned REST JSON APIs documented with OpenAPI 3.1.
Sets the interface standard and documentation approach.
Should schedules accept cron expressions, fixed intervals, or both?
Recommended: both, normalized internally to a schedule definition.
Defines scheduling API and validation behavior.
Which timezone should schedules use: per schedule, account timezone, or UTC?
Recommended: IANA timezone per schedule, defaulting to account timezone, with UTC storage.
Prevents ambiguous trigger times and daylight-saving errors.
What should happen if a scheduled run is active when the next occurrence arrives?
Choose per schedule: Skip, Queue, or Parallel. Recommended default: Skip.
Controls duplicate work and execution backlog.
What should happen to missed executions after downtime?
Choose Skip or Catch up. Recommended default: skip and record a misfire event.
Will the service run with multiple replicas, and may it use a clustered scheduler backed by PostgreSQL?
Recommended: yes; use clustered Quartz or an approved existing job platform.
Avoids duplicate firing and ensures high-availability scheduling.
Do schedules need start/end dates and a maximum execution count?
Recommended: optional start/end dates; optional maximum run count.
Supports bounded campaigns and operational control.
Which identity provider and token format should the service support?
Provide OIDC/OAuth2 details. Recommended: Spring Security resource server validating JWTs.
Authentication cannot be implemented safely without the trust source.
What JWT issuer, audience, and role/identity claim names should be validated?
Provide values or confirm configurable placeholders for local environments.
Defines token validation and identity extraction.
What roles and permissions are required?
Proposed roles: AGENT_VIEWER, AGENT_AUTHOR, AGENT_OPERATOR, AGENT_ADMIN; confirm permission matrix.
Creates the authorization model for each endpoint and action.
Are agents private to creators, shared within a team/account, or globally visible?
Recommended: account-scoped by default, with explicit owner and sharing metadata.
Defines data visibility and access checks.
Is the system multi-tenant, and which identifier establishes the tenant boundary?
Confirm WebEngage account, license code, workspace, or another immutable claim.
Tenant isolation must be embedded in every query and execution.
Can administrators read execution transcripts belonging to other users or tenants?
Recommended: tenant admins may read their tenant only; cross-tenant access requires an audited support role.
Transcripts can contain sensitive customer and platform data.
Should the initiating user’s identity and permissions be revalidated when a scheduled job runs later?
Recommended: validate the schedule owner and current permissions at execution time; define service-owner fallback explicitly.
Prevents schedules from retaining revoked privileges indefinitely.
Is service-to-service authentication required in addition to human-user authentication?
Recommended: yes; use workload identity or signed service tokens for internal callers.
Supports API-triggered automation without impersonating a person.
Where should per-run transcripts be stored?
Recommended: PostgreSQL for searchable metadata and messages initially; external object storage for oversized payloads if needed.
Storage choice shapes consistency, search, retention, and scale.
Which run events must be recorded?
Confirm trigger input, prompts, model responses, tool requests/results, retries/errors, final output, timing, and token usage.
Data Privacy / Compliance; Core Agentic Layer; Backend Engineering
Defines the authoritative execution history and debugging evidence.
May raw prompts and tool results be retained, or must sensitive fields be redacted or encrypted?
Recommended: classify fields; redact credentials; encrypt sensitive payloads; allow tool-specific redaction policies.
Security / IAM; Core Platform / Tool Owners
Prevents the log from becoming a sensitive-data liability.
What retention period applies to transcripts and audit events?
Specify separate retention for execution content and immutable audit metadata.
Controls storage sizing and compliance with deletion obligations.
Should transcript access require a separate permission?
Recommended: yes, separate VIEW_AGENT_TRANSCRIPT from VIEW_AGENT and RUN_AGENT.
Agent metadata is generally less sensitive than execution content.
Do stakeholders need searchable transcripts and a transcript retrieval API?
Recommended: filter by tenant, agent, run, status, initiator, and time range; avoid full-text search in the MVP unless required.
Are there compliance requirements for PII, data residency, encryption, legal hold, or deletion?
Provide applicable policies and approved storage regions/services.
May materially constrain architecture and operational procedures.
Should CRUD, publishing, scheduling, and manual-run actions have immutable audit records?
Recommended: yes, including actor, tenant, action, target, timestamp, correlation ID, and before/after summary.
Which database should the service target?
Determines persistence implementation and operational ownership.
Are Redis, Kafka, or another queue/job platform already available?
List approved shared infrastructure and usage constraints.
Avoids inventing infrastructure and guides asynchronous execution design.
For asynchronous runs, should the service use an existing job platform, Kafka, or a database-backed worker?
Recommended: approved enterprise job/queue platform; otherwise transactional database-backed outbox and workers for the first release.
Defines delivery guarantees, recovery, and scaling.
What is the deployment target: Kubernetes, VMs, or another environment?
Recommended: Kubernetes if it is the internal standard.
Determines packaging, health checks, scaling, and configuration.
Should delivery include Dockerfile, local Compose dependencies, health/readiness endpoints, and Kubernetes manifests?
Recommended: Dockerfile, local Compose, and Actuator probes; include manifests only if deployment conventions are provided.
Defines the deployable artifact and local developer experience.
Are there internal WebEngage libraries, parent POMs, API standards, or artifact repositories that must be used?
Provide references and version constraints before scaffolding.
Ensures the project fits internal engineering and supply-chain standards.
Are Java 21, Spring Boot 3.x, Spring Security, Spring Data JPA, PostgreSQL, Flyway, Quartz, and springdoc-openapi acceptable?
Recommended: yes, subject to WebEngage-supported versions and scheduler decision.
Locks the baseline stack and compatibility envelope.
Should the project use Maven or Gradle?
Recommended: Maven unless WebEngage standardizes on Gradle.
Determines build, dependency, and CI conventions.
What Java group/package name should be used?
Establishes stable namespace and artifact coordinates.
Should the project use Lombok, Java records/manual code, or another convention?
Recommended: records for immutable API DTOs; explicit entities; avoid Lombok unless it is an internal standard.
Keeps generated code aligned with maintainability conventions.
Is there a standard API response/error envelope and structured logging format to follow?
Provide examples; otherwise use RFC 9457 Problem Details and structured JSON logs.
Ensures consistency with internal clients and operations.
What peak concurrent executions, schedule count, and API traffic should the system support?
Provide expected, peak, and first-year growth estimates.
Capacity assumptions affect queueing, database, and concurrency design.
What rate limits are required per user, tenant, agent, or tool?
Recommended: configurable tenant and tool limits, with stricter limits on costly or mutating tools.
Protects shared services from abuse and noisy neighbors.
What availability target and maximum execution duration are required?
Provide SLOs; recommended initial maximum run duration is configurable with a hard cap.
Defines resilience, timeout, and operational investment.
Should an execution survive service restarts and resume from its last completed step?
Recommended: persist each orchestration step and resume safely for asynchronous runs.
What retry, backoff, and circuit-breaker behavior is expected for the Core Agentic Layer?
Recommended: bounded exponential backoff for transient failures, circuit breaker, and no retry for validation errors.
Prevents cascading failures and improves controlled recovery.
Which observability stack should be integrated?
Confirm Micrometer/Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, Datadog, or internal equivalents.
Determines metrics, trace, log, and dashboard integrations.
Should token usage, model latency, tool latency, success rate, and estimated cost be recorded?
Recommended: yes, tagged by tenant and agent with privacy-safe cardinality controls.
Core Agentic Layer; SRE / Infrastructure; Data Privacy / Compliance
Enables cost governance, performance tuning, and service reporting.
Should the first delivery be a production-oriented foundation or a smaller MVP?
Recommended: production-oriented vertical slice with a limited initial tool set.
Aligns implementation depth, timeline, and acceptance criteria.
Which automated test levels are required?
Recommended: unit, Spring integration, Testcontainers database, authorization, scheduler, and deterministic agent-loop tests.
Defines quality gates and delivery effort.
Is generated OpenAPI documentation sufficient, or are architecture and operational documents also required?
Recommended: OpenAPI plus architecture overview, data model, runbook, and extension guide.
Ensures the service can be adopted and operated by other teams.
Should the repository include sample agents and tools demonstrating the complete tool-calling loop?
Recommended: yes, one read-only example and one guarded mutating example.
Provides an executable reference for future agent and tool authors.
Is CI configuration required, and which platform should it target?
Provide the approved platform and required checks; recommended checks include build, tests, lint, dependency scan, and image scan.
Defines repeatable delivery and security gates.
Should backward-compatible API/database evolution and optimistic locking be included in the first version?
Recommended: versioned migrations and optimistic locking from the outset; API compatibility rules documented.
Reduces lost updates and unsafe future evolution.
